html:
The Kingdom of Cochin was a small Hindu kingdom on the Kerala coast around the port of Kochi. It lasted from about the 12th century until 1949 and appears on the 1783 and 1800 maps.

Cochin was long overshadowed by its rival, the Zamorin of Calicut. When Portugal arrived in 1500, Cochin's raja took its side, and the Portuguese built their first fort in India here. The Dutch East India Company took the port in 1663. Kochi was a mixed city: Syrian Christians, Muslims and an old Jewish community, whose Paradesi Synagogue dates from 1568.

In the 1770s Cochin paid tribute to Hyder Ali of Mysore. Raja Rama Varma, known as Sakthan Thampuran, ruled from 1790 to 1805 and accepted British protection in 1791. Cochin stayed a princely state under British India, and in 1949 it merged with Travancore, later forming the state of Kerala. See also Malabar.
